objective: Frozen computation: on the not-all-equal thread, a chain of knots sharing one distinction, the six-regular weave (L = 6, 9, 12) and a threshold-line control, test whether the differ count is built from unit steps (P1), skips no level from any start (P2), and what order betweenness gives from a start; bond distance and steps apart as references; exploratory census of all not-all-equal relations at n <= 6.
status: Supported 2026-11-17 (referee pending): frozen computation, 9 of 9 predictions held: on the thread (n = 30), a chain of 15 knots and the weave (L = 6, 9, 12, exact) no distinction lies strictly between two others in the disagreement count, it is not built from unit steps, the longest chain with flips is 4 (3 without the start's flip); tau equals steps apart on the knot chain and not on the thread or weave; weave rate 2/3 at one step, below 1/2 at every third distinction of a row; census: betweenness absent at n = 4, present in 732 / 1,023 and 87,924 / 97,248 relations at n = 5, 6; no line gap graph.
title: Does the differ count give an order with nothing skipped
